plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Clouds of blush-white, almond-scented blossoms cover the bare branches before the leaves open. Along the Tidal Basin, the petals drift down like confetti in the breeze and cover the paths and water in pale pink.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April. Peak bloom usually falls between the last week of March and the first week of April. It has ranged from mid-March to as late as April 18, so April 10 is often the tail end of the show.
plants.location: Washington, D.C., USA (Tidal Basin and National Mall)
plants.funFact: The first trees were planted in Washington in 1912 as a gift of friendship from Japan. Officials call it peak bloom once 70% of the Yoshino blossoms are open.

plants.name: Lupinus texensis
plants.description: This wildflower covers roadsides and open meadows in sheets of deep blue. Each flower spike is tipped with a small white cap that fades to magenta as the bloom ages. Photographers and families flock to the fields every spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peak bloom runs from late March to mid-April, which puts April 10 right in the middle of the season.
plants.location: Central Texas and the Texas Hill Country, USA
plants.funFact: Lupinus texensis became the Texas state flower in 1901 after it replaced Lupinus subcarnosus. In 1971 the legislature extended the honor to every bluebonnet species in the state.
